post.title: Do You Really Need an 850 Credit Score? The 780 Rule
post.ig:
You don't need a perfect 850 to get the best rates.
Only 1.71% of consumers had an 850 FICO Score in June 2026 (Experian).
Fannie Mae's top mortgage pricing tier starts at 780 (LLPA grid updated Sept. 30, 2026).
Our math: with 20% down on a $400,000 loan, a 780 and an 850 both pay a 0.375% fee, $1,500. Difference: $0.
Experian's top auto tier, super prime, starts at 781: 4.41% average new-car APR in Q2 2026.
Sources: Fannie Mae LLPA Matrix; Experian.
News and education, not financial advice.
